sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对健康的看法真的非常不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去非常专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我才意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现会好得多。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.

sentences.en: And I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开WHOOP应用，看看我的睡眠、压力、消耗是如何与我的心情、跑步表现以及我每天的感受相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么顶尖运动员，但我确实受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很享受更多地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And WHOOP also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions
sentences.zh: WHOOP还为我提供这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我更有意图性，这意味着我在日常生活中

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to the Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这个播客中，我们探讨二十岁时的一些重大生活变化

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 和人生转折，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we uncover the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身在世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听另一期节目，和我们一起探索二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about healing past trauma in a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈论的是在一段新恋情中治愈过去的创伤。

sentences.en: Romantic relationships in our 20s are so difficult because there is no guidebook to how we should be going about it.
sentences.zh: 我们二十岁的恋爱关系非常艰难，因为对于我们应该如何去做，并没有一本指南。

sentences.en: There are so many questions that go along with that, like, should I delete the dating apps and try and meet someone organically?
sentences.zh: 随之而来的有那么多问题，比如，我应该删掉约会软件，尝试通过自然的方式去认识某人吗？

sentences.en: How long does it take to get over someone?
sentences.zh: 忘记一个人需要多长时间？

sentences.en: When do I know it's time to break up with my significant other?
sentences.zh: 我怎么知道什么时候该和另一半分手？

sentences.en: But one of the biggest questions or conundrums I get all the time, which I will admit I've personally faced, is do you have to be healed before entering into a new relationship?
sentences.zh: 但我经常遇到、而且我也承认自己曾亲自面对的最大的问题或困惑之一是：在进入一段新恋情之前，你必须完全被治愈吗？

sentences.en: That is a massive question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: We undoubtedly carry baggage, trauma, memories, past experiences from the people we have dated and loved and been connected to.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们都带着包袱、创伤、记忆、以及来自我们曾经约会过、爱过和交往过的人的过去经验。

sentences.en: And some of that baggage is not great, is not pleasant.
sentences.zh: 其中一些包袱并不好，甚至令人不快。

sentences.en: And it's perhaps something that we're not ready to unpack yet.
sentences.zh: 这也许是我们还没准备好去剖析的东西。

sentences.en: But does that mean that if you have not done all the necessary healing, you should hold off on love?
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着，如果你还没有完成所有必要的治愈，你就应该暂缓去爱？

sentences.en: Or can you equally heal whilst being with someone new, someone who treats you well and helps you into that kind of self-acceptance, self-love journey?
sentences.zh: 还是说，你同样可以在与某个新人在一起的同时得到治愈——一个对你好、帮你走向自我接纳和自我爱恋之旅的人？

sentences.en: Today, we are joined by a brilliant guest who is going to talk us through a little bit about this very idea about healing, past trauma, and a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们邀请到了一位杰出的嘉宾，她将为我们详细讲解这个关于治愈、过去创伤以及新恋情的理念。

sentences.en: Welcome, Tasha, otherwise known as Real Talk TherapiSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎塔莎，也就是大家熟知的真实直言治疗师。

sentences.en: Thanks for joining us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So if people are not familiar with your work, you are incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以如果大家对你的工作还不太熟悉，你真的很棒。

sentences.en: You post this just amazing content that is factual, reasonable.
sentences.zh: 你发布的这些内容简直太棒了，既真实又讲道理。

sentences.en: You have, obviously, you have a therapy.
sentences.zh: 你显然从事心理治疗工作。

sentences.en: You are a therapist in your real life, in your life.
sentences.zh: 你在现实生活中就是一名治疗师。

sentences.en: Can you briefly introduce yourself and tell us about your work?
sentences.zh: 你能简要介绍一下你自己和你的工作吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I am a author, psychotherapist, and content creator.
sentences.zh: 我是一名作家、心理治疗师和内容创作者。

sentences.en: So I kind of, where it all started is I became a child and adolescent psychotherapist because I really want to work with children and trauma.
sentences.zh: 这一切的起点是，我成为了一名儿童和青少年心理治疗师，因为我真的很想和儿童以及创伤打交道。

sentences.en: And then I did my training and I realized that actually loads of adults have this little child in them that has a story to tell.
sentences.zh: 后来在我接受培训时，我意识到其实很多成年人内心都有一个有故事要讲的小孩。

sentences.en: And so I found myself working with adults and their past traumas.
sentences.zh: 于是我发现自己开始与成年人及其过去的创伤打交道。

sentences.en: And actually, particularly like on a topic, like you said, like a lot of people will find me when they're in a safe relationship and suddenly all their triggers are being pushed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如你所说，特别是在某个主题上，很多人会在他们处于一段安全的关系中时突然发现自己所有的情绪触发点都被戳中了。

sentences.en: And then we'll start to kind of work together to understand what that is and where that's coming from.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会开始一起努力去理解那是什么，以及它来自哪里。

sentences.en: And then I also have a social media platform where I share free content because obviously not everybody can access therapy, but everybody can access Instagram or TikTok.
sentences.zh: 我还拥有一个社交媒体平台，我在上面分享免费内容，因为显然不是每个人都能接受心理治疗，但每个人都能打开Instagram或TikTok。

sentences.en: So I do my best to share healing prompts, tips, and encouragement to anybody that needs it.
sentences.zh: 所以我尽最大努力向任何需要的人分享治愈提示、建议和鼓励。

sentences.en: And then obviously through my book as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有通过我的书。

sentences.en: For those of you who do not or have not read this book, it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 对于那些没有或还没读过这本书的人来说，它真的太棒了。

sentences.en: It's called, it's called Real Talk.
sentences.zh: 它叫做，它叫做《真实直言》（Real Talk）。

sentences.en: So like you'll be able to find it.
sentences.zh: 所以你们可以找到它。

sentences.en: And it's kind of like one of those books, we were talking about this before,
sentences.zh: 这就像是那种书，我们之前也讨论过这一点，

sentences.en: that everyone I think needs no matter how much therapy you have done because it will introduce you to just so many concepts around healing,
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都需要读，无论你已经做过多少次心理治疗，因为它会向你介绍关于治愈的如此多的概念，

sentences.en: around living your best life that we often don't think about.
sentences.zh: 关于过上最好生活的概念，而这些是我们经常不会去想的。

sentences.en: So I would very much recommend going out and grabbing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常推荐大家出去买一本。

sentences.en: And I just want to say thank you for coming on once again.
sentences.zh: 我只想说谢谢你再次来到节目中。

sentences.en: Obviously, we're talking about healing whilst in a new relationship.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们在谈论在一段新恋情中的治愈。

sentences.en: I think it is so interesting what you said about how a lot of people come to you and find you when they finally are in this like safe relationship.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你刚才说的话非常有意思，很多人在终于处于这种安全的关系中时才会来找你、发现你。

sentences.en: They're experiencing safe, healthy love for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们生平第一次体验到安全、健康的爱。

sentences.en: And that is scary to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是可怕的。

sentences.en: I feel like that's because a lot of past relationships and experiences can sometimes cause us harm.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是因为很多过去的恋情和经历有时会给我们带来伤害。

sentences.en: Like love is one of the most vulnerable things, one of the most vulnerable emotions that we can have.
sentences.zh: 就像爱是最脆弱的事情之一，是我们能拥有的最脆弱的情感之一。

sentences.en: And so there is going to be trauma that comes along with that.
sentences.zh: 所以随之而来的必然会有创伤。

sentences.en: I feel like anything that is beautiful always carries an undecided darkness or a way that it can be manipulated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得任何美好的事物总是带有某种未知的黑暗，或者说可能被操纵的方式。

sentences.en: What are some of the examples or maybe like instances of past trauma that you have come across that we tend to carry into new relationships?
sentences.zh: 你遇到过哪些过去创伤的例子或实例，是我们往往会带到新恋情中去的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a lot of the time when people think about trauma, they think of the really big things which obviously absolutely are valid types of trauma.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得很多时候当人们想到创伤时，他们会想到那些非常大的事情，这些当然绝对是有效且真实的创伤类型。

sentences.en: But it's not only those things that can be trauma that we carry.
sentences.zh: 但我们携带的创伤不只有这些。

sentences.en: So, yes, there could be things like abuse or neglect that we had from childhood or even in relationships that we had in adulthood.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，可能有一些事情，比如我们在童年时期或甚至在成年后的恋爱关系中遭受的虐待或忽视。

sentences.en: But there could also be really small traumas.
sentences.zh: 但也可能是一些非常小的创伤。

sentences.en: They call them little T's.
sentences.zh: 人们称它们为“小t创伤”（little t's）。

sentences.en: I think they call them, I've forgotten now, small T's, little T's.
sentences.zh: 我想他们是这么叫的，我有点记不清了，小t创伤。

sentences.en: And it could be as small as being a baby and having a parent who never picked you up when you were crying.
sentences.zh: 它可能小到作为一个婴儿时，父母在你哭泣时从不抱你。

sentences.en: And that might sound like a small thing at first, but actually it happens time and time again.
sentences.zh: 起初这听起来可能是一件小事，但实际上它一次又一次地发生。

sentences.en: You learn as a baby that nobody's there for me.
sentences.zh: 作为一个婴儿，你学会了没有人会在我身边。

sentences.en: Nobody can attend to my needs.
sentences.zh: 没有人能照顾我的需求。

sentences.en: And so I have to, you know, fend for myself.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须，你知道的，自力更生。

sentences.en: And so even those little small things or even a parent who doesn't give that much eye contact or a parent who calls you a crybaby as a child, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，即使是那些微小的事情，或者父母不怎么和你进行眼神交流，或者父母在小时候叫你爱哭鬼，你知道的，

sentences.en: you internalise all of these experiences and you expect them in your adult relationships, if that's a friendship or in your romantic relationships.
sentences.zh: 你把所有这些经历都内化了，并期望在你的成年关系中——无论是友情还是浪漫的恋爱关系中——也会遇到它们。

sentences.en: And then the other thing is that, you know, when you've had those traumas or those experiences, it kind of shapes your brain in a particular way.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，你知道，当你经历过这些创伤或经历时，它会以某种特定方式塑造你的大脑。

sentences.en: And so you, even though those things don't feel comfortable, they feel familiar.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管那些事情感觉并不舒服，但它们感觉很熟悉。

sentences.en: And so you find ways to reenact them.
sentences.zh: 因此，你会想方设法去重演它们。

sentences.en: One thing that I find when people are in a safe relationship,
sentences.zh: 我发现当人们处于一段安全的关系中时，有一件事会发生，

sentences.en: their brain starts to panic.
sentences.zh: 他们的大脑开始恐慌。

sentences.en: Like, wait, he texts me back?
sentences.zh: 比如，等等，他回我信息了？

sentences.en: Like, when I text, he texts me back.
sentences.zh: 就像，我发信息时，他回我信息了。

sentences.en: Like, what is going on?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Like, what is this about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是啥情况？

sentences.en: And we might get the ick or we might, you know, start to think that he's ingenuine or the person's ingenuine, but it's just the alarm system in our brain is saying,
sentences.zh: 我们可能会产生生理性厌恶（the ick），或者我们可能会，你知道的，开始觉得他不真诚或这个人不真诚，但这其实只是我们大脑中的警报系统在说：

sentences.en: this is very different and I don't know if I trust it yet.
sentences.zh: 这非常不同，我还不知道是否能信任它。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can often look like that.
sentences.zh: 是的，情况经常会是这样的。

sentences.en: That's actually so interesting because I've had that experience and you were saying, oh, they start like texting me back.
sentences.zh: 这其实真的很有趣，因为我有过这种经历，你刚才说，哦，他们开始回我信息。

sentences.en: They want to see me.
sentences.zh: 他们想见我。

sentences.en: And I remember when I, like, first started seeing my partner and he was so, like, adamant that he wanted to make plans and I was like, is this guy love bombing me?
sentences.zh: 我记得我刚开始和伴侣交往时，他非常坚定地想要做出计划，而我就在想：这家伙是在对进行爱情轰炸吗？

sentences.en: Like, is this guy a psychopath?
sentences.zh: 这家伙是个精神病吗？

sentences.en: Like, why does he want to see me so much?
sentences.zh: 为什么他这么想见我？

sentences.en: Like, what's his problem?
sentences.zh: 他有什么毛病？

sentences.en: But it's so true.
sentences.zh: 但这太真实了。

sentences.en: We are so used to what we feel, like, comfortable and familiar with that we try and recreate that because that is, like, the only reality that we've ever known.
sentences.zh: 我们太习惯于那些让我们感到舒适和熟悉的事物，以至于我们试图去重现它们，因为那是我们唯一知道的现实。

sentences.en: How does, like, these, because it's not just past relationship patterns, right?
sentences.zh: 这些是如何——因为这不仅仅是过去的恋爱模式，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I guess it is, it's past relationship patterns, but not just past romantic relationship patterns.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想是的，这就是过去的恋爱模式，但不仅仅是过去的浪漫恋爱模式。

sentences.en: It also has to do with the relationship we have with our parents, our family, our caregivers.
sentences.zh: 它还与我们和父母、家人、照顾者的关系有关。

sentences.en: How does some of this trauma impact our approach to dating or love, maybe through self-sabotage, self-abandonment, settling, a fear response like the one you spoke about?
sentences.zh: 其中一些创伤是如何影响我们对约会或爱情的态度的？也许是通过自我破坏、自我遗弃、将就、或者像你刚才说的那种恐惧反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, we, we kind of have, when this happens, we kind of have this unfinished business that needs to be, you know, resolved and usually, like, our inner child would be the one that
sentences.zh: 是的，我们，当这种情况发生时，我们内心会有一种未了的事情需要得到，你知道的，解决，通常情况下，我们的内在小孩会是那个

sentences.en: carries that unfinished business and tries to make sure that it's, it gets what it needs.
sentences.zh: 承载着这种未了心愿并试图确保它得到所需之物的人。

sentences.en: Um, but, yeah, often we don't know how to, we know, we know what we, we know what we want to receive.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，通常我们不知道如何去——我们知道，我们知道我们想要什么。

sentences.en: We know we want to receive, um, love or to, um, iron out unfinished business, but we don't know how to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们想要得到爱，或者去理清未了的事情，但我们不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: Um, and then that's where the kind of self-sabotaging or destructive, um, things can happen.
sentences.zh: 然后，这就是那些自我毁灭或破坏性的事情可能发生的地方。

sentences.en: One thing that I noticed that if we've had kind of, uh, a childhood where maybe our parents
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一件事是，如果我们经历过这样的童年：也许我们的父母

sentences.en: let us down or our families let us down in whatever way, many people will respond by being really hyper-vigilant, not hyper-vigilant, sorry.
sentences.zh: 让我们失望了，或者我们的家庭在某种程度上让我们失望了，许多人的反应是变得非常过度警惕——不是过度警惕，抱歉。

sentences.en: Many people will respond by being very hyper-independent when it comes to dating.
sentences.zh: 许多人在约会时表现得非常极度独立（hyper-independent）。

sentences.en: So they'll kind of say, oh, I don't need anybody or it's fine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会说，哦，我不需要任何人，这挺好的。

sentences.en: I'm going to, like, date loads of people, but they don't mean anything to me.
sentences.zh: 我要去和很多人约会，但他们对我来说没有任何意义。

sentences.en: Um, there's this kind of, like, almost like, I don't actually need that intimate, the intimacy, like, the intimacy that's just so above me.
sentences.zh: 有一种，几乎像是，我其实并不需要那种亲密感，那种亲密感对我来说太遥远了。

sentences.en: Um, and actually that's fair.
sentences.zh: 而实际上这很合理。

sentences.en: That's fair of getting too close to somebody because they might let you down and they might reject you.
sentences.zh: 为了避免与某人走得太近而可能让你失望并拒绝你，这是合理的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, and that's one way that it can kind of look is that we, yeah, we almost have this
sentences.zh: 这就是它可能表现出来的一种方式，我们，是的，我们几乎拥有这样一个

sentences.en: exterior, um, that we tell ourselves and exterior narrative that we tell ourselves that actually gets in the way of us actually receiving what we need and what we want.
sentences.zh: 外表，我们对自己讲述的外表和叙事，实际上阻碍了我们真正接受我们所需和想要的东西。

sentences.en: It sounds a lot like emotional unavailability to me, like, the sense of, like, I've been hurt in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像是情感上的不可接近，比如，我在过去受过伤。

sentences.en: We are so hyper-vigilant towards threats that may hurt us again in the future that we eliminate any possibility for that.
sentences.zh: 我们对未来可能再次伤害我们的威胁高度警惕，以至于我们消除了这种可能性的任何迹象。

sentences.en: Some of those possibilities, some of those opportunities are actually quite positive, would actually be able to rewire our brain, change our mind.
sentences.zh: 其中一些可能性，一些机会其实是相当积极的，实际上能够重塑我们的大脑，改变我们的想法。

sentences.en: It's really interesting what you talk about in terms of the hyper-independence, because
sentences.zh: 你谈到极度独立（hyper-independence）时非常有意思，因为

sentences.en: I think that that is a way past trauma shows up in our relationships that is not often recognized
sentences.zh: 我认为这是过去创伤在我们的关系中表现出来的一种方式，却往往不被认识到，

sentences.en: because independence is such a celebrated trait in our society, especially in, like, Western
sentences.zh: 因为独立在我们社会中是一个备受赞誉的特质，尤其是在西方

sentences.en: societies, especially in individualistic societies, whereby being able to, like, provide for yourself,
sentences.zh: 社会中，尤其是在个人主义社会中，能够自给自足、

sentences.en: be your own emotional security, your own sense of comfort, make all the money that you need is, like, super admirable.
sentences.zh: 成为自己的情感安全感来源、自己的舒适感来源、赚取你需要的所有钱，被认为超级令人钦佩。

sentences.en: But I think it overlooks this thing of you do need a community, you do need love and connection to sustain yourself in a way.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它忽视了这样一点：在某种程度上，你确实需要一个社群，你确实需要爱和连接来维持生存。

sentences.en: So how do you think, you know, if you've recognized that you are hyper-independent, how do you almost
sentences.zh: 所以你认为，如果你意识到自己是极度独立的，你该如何几乎

sentences.en: stop doing that, like, it's such a deeply ingrained behavior, how do you unlearn those behaviors?
sentences.zh: 停止这样做？这是一种根深蒂固的行为，你该如何改掉这些行为？

sentences.en: I think it's about kind of asking yourself the question of what would it be like to receive something that is soft and warm and light and loving?
sentences.zh: 我认为这在于问自己这样一个问题：接受一些柔软、温暖、光明和充满爱意的东西会是什么样的体验？

sentences.en: What would that actually feel like?
sentences.zh: 那到底会是什么感觉？

sentences.en: And what ways am I likely to reject it or stop it or block it?
sentences.zh: 我可能会在哪些方面拒绝它、阻止它或阻碍它？

sentences.en: Like, just kind of noticing it, I think, is the first thing and just being aware of, like, what it looks like when you receive those things.
sentences.zh: 我认为，去注意到它就是第一步，并意识到当你接受这些东西时它是什么样子的。

sentences.en: Like, when a friend gives you a compliment, how do you respond?
sentences.zh: 比如，当一个朋友赞美你时，你是如何回应的？

sentences.en: When a friend says, call me whenever you need anything and then you suddenly need something and you still don't call, like, what is that about?
sentences.zh: 当朋友对你说“需要什么随时给我打电话”，结果你突然有需要了却还是没打，这到底是怎么回事呢？

sentences.en: So I think it's, like, noticing those things of, like, how you stop yourself from receiving
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这就像是去注意到那些你是如何阻止自己去接受

sentences.en: what you actually do deserve, but you're telling yourself that you don't need it for whatever reason.
sentences.zh: 那些你其实完全应得的东西，但你却在找各种理由告诉自己你并不需要它。

sentences.en: And then I talk a lot about leaning into the cringe.
sentences.zh: 然后我经常谈到的一点就是去正视并接纳那种尴尬感。

sentences.en: Like, a lot of people, I think, I believe that the things that we cringe at are the things that we actually desperately need, but we're too scared to say.
sentences.zh: 就像很多人，我认为，我坚信让我们感到尴尬的事恰恰是我们内心极度渴望，却又羞于说出口的。

sentences.en: So whether it's cringing at a couple, PDA-ing and hugging and kissing on the road, maybe that's something that we actually do want to receive, but we're like, ew, that's gross.
sentences.zh: 所以不管是看到情侣在大街上搂搂抱抱、卿卿我我而感到尴尬，也许那正是我们内心其实很想得到的体验，但我们却会觉得，咦，真恶心。

sentences.en: I'd never want that.
sentences.zh: 我才永远不要那样。

sentences.en: Like, maybe you do.
sentences.zh: 但说不定，你其实是想要的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Salmon that a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 再稍微深入剖析一下这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think, like, noticing when you have those cringey feelings and maybe questioning what is the need underneath that that I might be communicating through my cringe.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，去注意你产生那些尴尬情绪的时刻，并试着去质疑：潜藏在尴尬背后的、我可能正在表达的需求到底是什么？

sentences.en: When you said that, I was like, wow, that is, I actually think that is so accurate.
sentences.zh: 你刚才那么说的时候，我就想，哇，真的，我甚至觉得这简直太准确了。

sentences.en: Because the other example I always think of is, like, cringing at people who, you know, like, kind of, like, always validate their partner, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我脑海中总会想起的另一个例子是，对那些你知道的、总是无时无刻不在肯定自己伴侣的人感到尴尬，对吧？

sentences.en: I remember seeing this couple on TikTok a little while ago and it, like, went kind of viral.
sentences.zh: 我记得不久前在TikTok上看到过这样一对情侣，当时还挺火的。

sentences.en: It was this example of them doing, like, a love surge.
sentences.zh: 那是他们展示某种“爱意大爆发”的一个例子。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've seen this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有看过这个。

sentences.en: Do you know what I'm talking about?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'll send it to you because it's this really, like, lighthearted video where this couple is, like, when one of us feels a lot of love, we get this thing called a
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我回头把视频发给你，因为那是一个非常轻松有趣的视频，视频里这对情侣说，当其中一人感受到浓浓爱意时，我们就会产生一种叫做

sentences.en: love surge and we have to, like, hug each other and whatnot.
sentences.zh: “爱意大爆发”的体验，然后我们就必须拥抱彼此之类的。

sentences.en: And all of these people were like, that is so cringe.
sentences.zh: 结果所有人都评论说：这太尴尬了。

sentences.en: Like, that is so disgusting.
sentences.zh: 简直太让人下头了。

sentences.en: That is, like, revolting.
sentences.zh: 简直让人作呕。

sentences.en: And I remember watching that feeling that way and then obviously met my partner and was like, I get that.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时看的时候也是这种感觉，但后来理所当然地遇到了我的伴侣，就觉得：我懂了。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我完全懂了。

sentences.en: I wanted that.
sentences.zh: 我当时就渴望这个。

sentences.en: I wanted to be that loved that someone was willing to, like, put that online for me.
sentences.zh: 我渴望被那样去爱——甚至有人愿意为我把这种爱发到网上。

sentences.en: So it is, like, a very interesting thing how our brain tries to, like, trick us out of recognising our needs as, like, a protective mechanism in some ways.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一件非常有趣的事，我们的脑海如何试图通过欺骗我们来让我们忽视自己的需求，在某种程度上这其实是一种保护机制。

sentences.en: Do you think there are other, like, defence mechanisms as well that we kind of put up?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们身上是不是还有其他类似这样的防卫机制呢？

sentences.en: Other than cringe is a big one, I think.
sentences.zh: 除了“尴尬”算是一个重灾区之外，我觉得。

sentences.en: Are there any others that, like, we might not be able to recognise?
sentences.zh: 还有没有其他我们可能自己都觉察不到的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, like, there's obviously we can obviously, like, deny what we need or but I think also, like, the role that we play with that person.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得，很显然我们当然会去否定自己真正需要的东西，但我觉得这也体现在我们跟那个人相处时所扮演的角色上。

sentences.en: Like, if we're dating someone, some of us will, if we have childhood wounds or relationship wounds, we might find ourselves wanting to be rescued by our new partner or for them to
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我们正在跟某人约会，如果我们带着童年创伤或情感创伤，我们可能会发现自己极度渴望被新伴侣拯救，或者希望他们

sentences.en: suddenly fulfil all of our needs.
sentences.zh: 能突然满足我们所有的需求。

sentences.en: Every single need we've ever had in our lifetime, we want this partner to fulfil for us, which is impossible and, you know, poor person to have to have such a huge responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我们这辈子产生过的每一个需求，都想让这个伴侣来满足，这其实是不可能的，而且说实话，要求另一个人承担这么巨大的责任对他太不公平了。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it can feel like, oh, suddenly there's someone, a hero here who can fulfil everything
sentences.zh: 但是，没错，这确实会让人觉得，哦，突然之间出现了一个英雄，他能满足我

sentences.en: that I need and that means that we put them on a pedestal and we expect them to be really perfect and when they make a mistake, it's absolutely devastating to us.
sentences.zh: 需要的一切，这意味着我们会把他们高高捧上神坛，期望他们十全十美，而当他们犯错时，我们会感到彻底的崩溃。

sentences.en: I think, and this is different to, like, non-negotiable mistakes, like, if it was something huge, like, they were unfaithful, that's different.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这和那些不可妥协的原则性错误是两回事，比如如果发生了出轨这种大事，那性质就不一样了。

sentences.en: But if it's, like, a mistake, like, they didn't respond to your emotions the way that you wanted them to, but you hadn't told them how you want them to respond to your emotions,
sentences.zh: 但如果只是一些小错误，比如他们没有按你期望的方式回应你的情绪，可你之前根本没告诉过他们你希望他们如何回应你的情绪，

sentences.en: things like that, it's, like, we do need those mistakes to happen because then we can grow the relationship and they can learn about you, you can learn about them.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情，其实我们真的需要这些错误发生，因为只有这样我们才能让感情成长，他们能借此更了解你，你也能更了解他们。

sentences.en: But for some people, it's, like, no, I'm done, I'm out.
sentences.zh: 但对某些人来说，情况却是：不，我受够了，我直接走人。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, I think it's that how we deal with mistakes our partner makes and how we put them on a pedestal is also a big one as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我觉得我们如何处理伴侣犯的错以及我们如何将他们奉若神明，这也是一个非常普遍且重要的问题。

sentences.en: I can, once again, agree with that.
sentences.zh: 这一点我再次举双手赞同。

sentences.en: Something that's really interesting about that is, like, the nitpicking and the sense of, like, if this love isn't perfect, I don't want it and constantly looking for problems
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有一个非常有趣的现象，就是挑剔心理，以及那种“如果这份爱不够完美，那我宁可不要”的心态，并且不断去寻找那些

sentences.en: that actually are not probleMs.
sentences.zh: 其实根本算不上问题的问题。

sentences.en: Sometimes they're just an excuse for us to leave because we're feeling vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 有时这些不过是我们想要离开的借口，因为我们感到了脆弱。

sentences.en: When you talked about that of, like, oh, my partner hasn't responded to my emotional needs, but I've never told them why, or small things like, oh, they didn't text me back
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才提到的，哦，我的伴侣没有回应我的情感需求，但我从来没告诉过他们为什么；或者一些小事，比如，哦，他们没有在两小时内

sentences.en: within, like, two hours, they must hate me, the relationship is over.
sentences.zh: 回我信息，他们一定恨我，这段感情完蛋了。

sentences.en: And you could sometimes tell yourself, like, well, that's a non-negotiable for me, when actually it's just you feeling quite triggered by their response.
sentences.zh: 有时你会对自己说，好吧，这触及了我的底线，而实际上，只不过是他们的反应触动了你的情绪触发点（triggered）。

sentences.en: And it's really more symbolic of something deeper.
sentences.zh: 这其实更深层次地象征着某些东西。

sentences.en: Like, you are actually not ready for this, you're not, you're not prepared to be vulnerable with them.
sentences.zh: 比如，你其实根本还没准备好面对这一切，你并没有、没有准备好向他们展露脆弱。

sentences.en: So I think it's actually really interesting because this really leads into my next question, the sense of, like, a healthy relationship will challenge you.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这真的很有趣，因为这直接引出了我的下一个问题：那种健康的亲密关系一定会挑战你。

sentences.en: It will cause you to question how you perhaps approached love in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它会让你开始质疑自己过去对待爱的方式。

sentences.en: Do you think that there is a necessary level of healing we need to do before getting into a new relationship, or is there, like, we can, is it that, so that we can just heal in
sentences.zh: 你认为在进入一段新感情之前，我们是否需要完成一定程度的疗愈？还是说，我们可以直接在

sentences.en: another relationship straight off the bat?
sentences.zh: 另一段感情中顺理成章地开始边谈边疗愈？

sentences.en: Oh, I think a bit of both.
sentences.zh: 哦，我觉得这两者都有吧。

sentences.en: I'll do a little bit of sharing here.
sentences.zh: 在这里我也来分享一点我自己的经历。

sentences.en: So I actually got married this year, like, literally.
sentences.zh: 其实我今年刚刚结婚，真的是字面意义上的今年。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜恭喜。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, that's so exciting.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，太令人激动了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Wow, so fun.
sentences.zh: 哇，太棒了。

sentences.en: And I actually met my husband when we were 18, but it didn't work out.
sentences.zh: 其实我跟我先生18岁就认识了，但当时没能走到一起。

sentences.en: And then we reconnected when we were 28.
sentences.zh: 后来在我们28岁的时候又重新联系上了。

sentences.en: That is a love story.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是爱情小说本说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: And for it to actually, when we reconnected, everything just made so much sense.
sentences.zh: 而且神奇的是，当我们重新联系上时，一切都变得那么顺理成章。

sentences.en: But by that time, I had had five years of therapy.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，我已经接受了五年的心理治疗。

sentences.en: He had not had therapy before, but he had gone through a really big life-changing thing that had happened for him.
sentences.zh: 他虽然以前没做过心理治疗，但他经历了一件对他人生产生重大改变的事情。

sentences.en: And so we had both changed in a way.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都在某种程度上发生了改变。

sentences.en: We were still the same people, but we had a new emotional maturity.
sentences.zh: 我们虽然还是原来的我们，但我们拥有了全新的情感成熟度。

sentences.en: Whereas when we were 18, we were so emotionally immature.
sentences.zh: 而回想18岁的时候，我们实在太不成熟了。

sentences.en: Nothing could have seriously happened at that time.
sentences.zh: 在那个年纪，根本不可能有什么好结果。

sentences.en: But I think there is something of, like, some healing does have to take place.
sentences.zh: 但我认为确实存在这样一种情况：某种程度的疗愈是必须要发生的。

sentences.en: Some kind of self-awareness has to take place for you to be, or to even just start that self-awareness journey is a great bonus.
sentences.zh: 你必须具备某种自我觉察，或者哪怕只是开始踏上这段自我觉察之旅，也是一个极大的加分项。

sentences.en: It's like, to then be able to go into a relationship with somebody else who's also going to have all their own stuff, all their own histories, all their own baggage.
sentences.zh: 这样你才能带着这种状态进入与另一个人的关系中，而对方也必然带着他自己的一堆故事、历史和情感包袱。

sentences.en: And almost when you're in a relationship, it's almost like there's all this junk on the floor.
sentences.zh: 而且当你们真正进入一段关系时，感觉就像是地上散落着一堆杂物。

sentences.en: And you've got to work out together.
sentences.zh: 你们必须一起去清理、去分辨。

sentences.en: Okay, that one is mine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这个是我的。

sentences.en: I'll take this.
sentences.zh: 这个我来拿。

sentences.en: This bet is yours.
sentences.zh: 这个部分是你的。

sentences.en: That's mine.
sentences.zh: 那个是我的。

sentences.en: That's mine.
sentences.zh: 那个也是我的。

sentences.en: And you're almost like looking at the mess in between you and working out, divvying up.
sentences.zh: 你们就像是在审视彼此之间的这一团乱麻，然后一起动手把它们理清楚、分配好。

sentences.en: Okay, what is the stuff that I'm taking accountability for?
sentences.zh: 好吧，哪些是我应该承担责任的部分？

sentences.en: And what stuff are you taking accountability for?
sentences.zh: 哪些又是你应该承担责任的部分？

sentences.en: But if we don't have that self-awareness, we can't do that.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们缺乏这种自我觉察，我们就无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: We'll be like, oh, that stuff is all yours.
sentences.zh: 我们会变成这样：哦，这些乱七八糟的全都是你的。

sentences.en: That's like, none of that's mine.
sentences.zh: 这跟我一点关系都没有。

sentences.en: I've got nothing to do with all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 这些破事儿全赖不到我头上。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That's so true.
sentences.zh: 太真实了。

sentences.en: Also, that is such a beautiful story that you met at 18.
sentences.zh: 而且，你们18岁相识这个故事真的太美好了。

sentences.en: And it shows that like people can change, but they can change in parallel.
sentences.zh: 这也说明了人是会变的，而且他们可以朝着同频的方向改变。

sentences.en: Or like change in a way that looks different from the outside, but it makes them more compatible.
sentences.zh: 或者说，虽然从外表上看他们的改变方式可能不尽相同，但那却让他们变得更加契合。

sentences.en: I think it's a really, that's a really beautiful story in terms of also like how people can change in a relationship alongside each other, even if it looks different.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常非常美好的故事，特别是关于人们如何在一段关系中彼此相伴、共同成长，哪怕成长的方式看起来并不一样。

sentences.en: So congratulations on getting married.
sentences.zh: 所以再次恭喜你新婚快乐。

sentences.en: That's so amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真的太棒了。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式有了非常大的改变。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去总是执着于追求极限和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我终于意识到，如果我倾听身体的真实需求，我的状态反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我对我的Whoop爱不释手。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know, I'm such a data and information driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，各位，你们也知道，我是一个极度依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢打开Whoop应用，看我的睡眠、压力和身体负荷是如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我每天的整体状态相互关联的了。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝算不上什么顶尖运动员，但我确实从中获益良多。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很享受去更深入地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day to day about what I need,
sentences.zh: Whoop还为我提供了这些可执行的、个性化的深度洞察，这让我做起事来更有意向性，也意味着我在每天的生活中，能够针对自己的需求做出更明智的决定，

sentences.en: rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 而不是只知道盲目踩下油门，一路狂奔、狂奔、狂奔、狂奔。

sentences.en: There will be chanting.
sentences.zh: 这里会有整齐划一的助威。

sentences.en: There will be entire nations losing their voices at once.

sentences.en: If you can't beat the noise, come and bring it.

sentences.zh: 联合杯，肯·罗斯沃尔体育场，1月2日至10日。

sentences.zh: 网球，燃爆全场。

sentences.en: I think we're going to track back now because, like, we're talking about marriage.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在要把话题绕回去了，因为刚才聊到了婚姻。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about the opposite.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要聊聊跟它完全相反的话题。

sentences.en: I think sometimes people jump from one relationship to another very quickly to avoid healing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有时候人们为了逃避疗愈，会非常迅速地从一段感情跳进另一段感情。

sentences.en: Is that something that you've seen?
sentences.zh: 这种情况你见过吗？

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这背后的原因是什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm actually currently reading a book.
sentences.zh: 对，其实我目前正在读一本书。

sentences.en: It's called Really Good Actually.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《其实真的很好》（Really Good Actually）。

sentences.en: It's literally called Really Good Actually.
sentences.zh: 它的名字就叫《其实真的很好》。

sentences.en: Really Good Actually.
sentences.zh: 《其实真的很好》。

sentences.en: And it's about a woman who is in a relationship from age like 18 and they get married at 28 and then they get divorced two years later.
sentences.zh: 讲的是一个女性从18岁左右就开始谈恋爱，28岁结婚，结果两年后又离婚的故事。

sentences.en: So it's like a huge, it's a huge trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一个巨大的、沉重的打击。

sentences.en: But she goes through a phase of just dating constantly, constantly dating.
sentences.zh: 但她经历了一个疯狂约会、不断约会的阶段。

sentences.en: And I think it's that thing of, like, emotional availability to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这其实就是关于我们对内心的情感可及性（emotional availability）的问题。

sentences.en: It is, we, when we end a relationship or leave a relationship, we actually do have to be in a space of aloneness that a lot of us are terrified of.
sentences.zh: 当我们结束一段关系或离开一段感情时，我们确实需要进入一段独处的空间，而这正是我们许多人极其恐惧的。

sentences.en: And we're taught that aloneness is, you know, the worst thing anyone could experience and that we should avoid being alone at all times.
sentences.zh: 社会灌输给我们的观念是，独处是人能经历的最糟糕的事情，我们应该在任何时候都避免孤身一人。

sentences.en: Like, there's a whole air about being alone.
sentences.zh: 社会对“单身”似乎带有一种全方位的负面气场。

sentences.en: And I think even, like, a lot of single people that I know and friends that I know often feel quite judged for being single at a particular age because of this kind of judgment.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，甚至包括我认识的很多单身人士和朋友，由于这种外界的评判，往往会在达到某个特定年龄还单身时感到饱受审视。

sentences.en: And so I think when we are finally alone, first we have to sit with that, oh, I'm alone, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得当我们终于独自一人时，首先我们必须去直面那种“哦，我孤身一人了，这到底意味着什么”的感觉。

sentences.en: But also we have to sit with all the grief of grieving that relationship.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我们还必须去消化因哀悼这段逝去的感情而带来的所有悲伤。

sentences.en: And when we are grieving a relationship, it often brings up other experiences of grief that we've had in our lives.
sentences.zh: 当我们为一段感情感到悲伤时，它往往会勾起我们在生活中经历过的其他悲伤体验。

sentences.en: So if we've lost a parent or a friend or if we, you know, we're also grieving the part of ourselves that was in that relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们失去过父母或朋友，或者如果我们也在为曾经深处那段关系中的那个自己感到惋惜。

sentences.en: Or the life stages that we went through in that relationship, we're grieving a lot, basically.
sentences.zh: 或者是怀念我们在那段感情中经历过的人生阶段，总之，我们需要哀悼的东西实在太多了。

sentences.en: And nobody wants to sit in their grief.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人愿意沉浸在悲伤之中。

sentences.en: Like, it's not the most fun thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这绝对算不上什么令人愉快的体验。

sentences.en: And also we live in a culture which is, you know, grief avoidant.
sentences.zh: 并且我们生活在一个习惯于回避悲伤的文化环境中。

sentences.en: We don't like to talk about death or losses or endings.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢谈论死亡、失去或结局。

sentences.en: We just move on to the next thing.
sentences.zh: 我们只会急着翻篇，开启下一段旅程。

sentences.en: And I think that's where then there's this idea of like, okay, there's a song, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这就是为什么会出现那种想法，比如，有一首歌是这么唱的吧？

sentences.en: And there's, and then like a, I can't remember her name now, but there's a song that's like, move on to the next one or something.
sentences.zh: 然后还有，我一时想不起她叫什么名字了，但有一首歌大概是说“赶紧奔赴下一个”之类的话。

sentences.en: There's like, yeah, there's like so many phrases of like, if one thing doesn't work out, move on to the next thing.
sentences.zh: 就好像，对啊，有很多这样的说法，比如说，如果一件事行不通，就进入下一件事。

sentences.en: And that's what we tend to do.
sentences.zh: 我们通常也是这么做的。

sentences.en: Oh, it's like, Thank You Next by Ariana Grande.
sentences.zh: 哦，就像爱莉安娜·格兰德的《谢谢你，下一个》那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Is it that?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I was like racking my brain.
sentences.zh: 我当时绞尽脑汁。

sentences.en: So it's like, yeah, it's our way of coping, but it's obviously not great for us in the long run.
sentences.zh: 所以就像，对，这是我们应对的方式，但从长远来看，这显然对我们没有好处。

sentences.en: It's, it's just a temporary, a temporary distraction.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种暂时的、暂时的分心。

sentences.en: And avoidance as well.
sentences.zh: 也是一种逃避。

sentences.en: When you said it, sometimes we're so afraid of being alone and we're afraid of our solitude.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，有时我们太害怕孤独，也害怕独处。

sentences.en: If you have been in a relationship for a while, or if you've been in an unhealthy relationship where there has been so much intensity,
sentences.zh: 如果你谈了一段时间恋爱，或者经历过那种充满紧张感的不健康关系，

sentences.en: you're almost like addicted to this other person.
sentences.zh: 你几乎会对这个人上瘾。

sentences.en: You're addicted to the excitement, the feeling, the passion, whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 你对这种兴奋感、感觉、激情，无论你想怎么称呼它，都上了瘾。

sentences.en: And when that ends, there is a huge hole left behind, a huge, you almost are like in the state of like withdrawal or detox,
sentences.zh: 当这一切结束时，心里会留下一个巨大的空洞，一个巨大的空洞，你几乎处于一种戒断或排毒的状态，

sentences.en: where you are craving like the kind of connection that you previously had.
sentences.zh: 你会渴望那种你以前拥有过的连接感。

sentences.en: You're craving that love.
sentences.zh: 你渴望那种爱。

sentences.en: And so the first person that walks along, you're like, you, you will do just fine.
sentences.zh: 于是当第一个路过的人出现时，你会觉得，行吧，你就凑合吧。

sentences.en: Like you are like, who needs therapy when I can, someone else can like be a distraction for me.
sentences.zh: 你会想，谁还需要心理咨询，找个人来分散我的注意力不就行了。

sentences.en: So I think that's like something that I see quite a lot, especially in our twenties when it is so easy to find people who want to casually date you,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一种我经常看到的现象，尤其是在我们二十多岁的时候，很容易找到只想随便约会的人，

sentences.en: like who aren't looking for commitment, who are just down for a fun time.
sentences.zh: 那些不寻求承诺、只想找乐子的人。

sentences.en: You can go on a dating app.
sentences.zh: 你可以用交友软件。

sentences.en: And especially if you're a woman, like you can find someone pretty quickly who will at least like want to get a drink.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你是个女性，你能挺快地找到一个至少想跟你喝一杯的人。

sentences.en: So it's easy.
sentences.zh: 所以这很容易。

sentences.en: And that's such a distraction.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种很好的分散注意力的方式。

sentences.en: It's such like a mask, a facade that we put up where it's like, if I don't have to see my trauma, I don't have to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一层面具，一层我们戴上的伪装，仿佛在说，如果我不用去面对我的创伤，我就不用去处理它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think particularly for women or non-binary people, like that can be super liberating because, you know, we live in such a patriarchal, misogynist world.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，特别是对女性或非二元性别者来说，这会超级解压，因为你知道，我们生活在一个父权制、厌女的世界里。

sentences.en: But suddenly you can go into an app where you have access to so many potential suitors and you decide who you get to see when you see them, how often you see them.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，你可以登录一个软件，里面有大量潜在的追求者，你可以决定什么时候见谁、见他们多久、多久见一次。

sentences.en: Like it can feel when you've just gone through a breakup where you feel actually quite helpless or with your feelings, like I'm having to hold all these annoying, frustrating,
sentences.zh: 当刚经历分手而感到非常无助，或者面对内心的情绪不知所措时，比如我不得不承受所有这些烦人、沮丧、

sentences.en: sad feelings.
sentences.zh: 悲伤的情绪。

sentences.en: What do I do with them?
sentences.zh: 我该拿它们怎么办？

sentences.en: I feel helpless.
sentences.zh: 我感到无能为力。

sentences.en: I know I can feel more liberated and, you know, more productive by dating lots of people.
sentences.zh: 我知道通过和许多人约会，我可以感到更解放，你知道，也更充实。

sentences.en: It's almost like, you know, yeah, shifting the energy.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是，你知道的，对，转换一下能量。

sentences.en: That is so true and so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太对了，而且太迷人了。

sentences.en: I think you point out something really interesting where it's like you don't feel in control over the last relationship.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你指出了一点非常有趣，那就是你觉得自己对上一段感情失去了掌控感。

sentences.en: So you want to feel more in control.
sentences.zh: 所以你想找回掌控感。

sentences.en: You want to feel more in control.
sentences.zh: 你想重新获得掌控感。

sentences.en: This like these apps, this like dating system allows you to feel that way, even if it is just like temporary, even if it is a little bit of delusion.
sentences.zh: 这些软件，这种约会系统让你能够拥有这种感觉，哪怕它只是暂时的，哪怕带有一点自我欺骗。

sentences.en: So say you are someone who has you broken up with your partner.
sentences.zh: 假设你是一个刚刚和伴侣分手的人。

sentences.en: There has been things in that past relationship that maybe you haven't healed from.
sentences.zh: 在过去的感情中，有些事情你可能还没有完全释怀。

sentences.en: Maybe they cheated on you.
sentences.zh: 也许他们对你不忠。

sentences.en: Maybe they were not particularly kind to you.
sentences.zh: 也许他们对你并不是特别好。

sentences.en: Maybe they maybe it was like a situation ship and someone has just treated you poorly,
sentences.zh: 也许这只是一段暧昧关系，而对方待你很差，

sentences.en: hasn't it made you feel like you never really deserved anything more and you find someone amazing.
sentences.zh: 让你觉得你从来不配得到更好的，然后你遇到了一个很棒的人。

sentences.en: What are some of the things to look out for in a new relationship that indicate that you have some work to do that?
sentences.zh: 在一段新恋情中，有哪些迹象表明你还有一些心结需要去解开？

sentences.en: Maybe I'm going to use the analogy you gave before.
sentences.zh: 也许我要用你之前给过的那个比喻。

sentences.en: There is some junk on the floor that you need to to pick up.
sentences.zh: 地上有一些你需要捡起来的垃圾。

sentences.en: But I think I guess one thing is noticing you kind of named it earlier, like if you're picking at things, if you're picking at this is a hard one,
sentences.zh: 但我猜有一点就是要注意——你刚才其实也提到了——如果你在挑刺，如果你在挑刺，这就很难了，

sentences.en: because obviously we talk about red flags and we talk about, you know, obviously being quite hypervigilant to if the person you're dating is right for you.
sentences.zh: 因为显然我们谈论红线，谈论要保持高度警惕，看看约会对象是否适合你。

sentences.en: But picking at things is almost like it's almost like so my supervisor calls it a now a now story.
sentences.zh: 但挑刺几乎就像是，我的督导现在管这叫“当下故事”。

sentences.en: So it's almost like you're seeing something in a now, but actually has nothing to do what's happening now.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎就像你在当下看到了某些东西，但实际上它跟现在发生的事情毫无关系。

sentences.en: It's everything to do what's happening in your paSt.
sentences.zh: 它完全跟你过去发生的事情有关。

sentences.en: So maybe you're with someone and they looked at someone passing by, but for you,
sentences.zh: 所以也许你和某人在一起，他们看了一眼路过的人，但对你来说，

sentences.en: it triggered you to think about the time when your ex was looking at other people or dating other people behind your back.
sentences.zh: 这触动了你的回忆，让你想起了前任背着你偷偷看别人或跟别人约会的场景。

sentences.en: You know, there's this thing of like you start to merge the two realities together.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你会把这两种现实交织在一起。

sentences.en: So I think just noticing when you are picking at things, really ask yourself first, where is that coming from?
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，只要注意到自己在挑刺时，首先要认真问问自己，这到底是从哪来的？

sentences.en: Is it really, you know, from the now or is it potentially from the past or is it both?
sentences.zh: 它真的源于当下，还是可能源于过去，或者两者兼有？

sentences.en: I think the other thing is to notice when you feel safe and when you don't feel safe.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一件事是去觉察你什么时候感到安全，什么时候感到不安全。

sentences.en: So some people, they find that they feel absolutely safe with their new person, but it's when they're apart that they don't feel safe and they start to question things.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人发现，和新对象在一起时他们感到绝对安全，但只要一分开，他们就会感到不安并开始产生质疑。

sentences.en: And that might be your kind of history of, you know, absence.
sentences.zh: 这可能源于你对“缺失”的经历。

sentences.en: If you've had parents that are quite absent or if you had a partner that was quite absent,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾有经常缺席的父母，或者曾经有过一个总是缺席的伴侣，

sentences.en: it's going to give you lots of kind of feelings of anxiety when you're away from your new boo, basically.
sentences.zh: 那么当你离开你的新对象时，基本上会产生很多焦虑的情绪。

sentences.en: So just kind of when that happens, use that as a time to journal and think about where is that coming from and where else have you experienced that in your life as well?
sentences.zh: 所以当这种情况发生时，把它当作一个写日记的机会，思考一下这情绪是从哪里来的，你在生活的其他地方是否也经历过类似的事情？

sentences.en: That is incredibly relevant to me when I was like, I'm just sharing so much, Tasha.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说太有共鸣了，我当时就想，塔莎，我分享得太多了。

sentences.en: I'm just using you for free therapy.
sentences.zh: 我只是在白嫖你的免费心理咨询。

sentences.en: That's obviously what, that's what this sounds like at this point.
sentences.zh: 发展到这一步，听起来显然就是这样。

sentences.en: But I remember when I would be like totally fine when we were around each other.
sentences.zh: 但我记得我们在一起的时候我完全没问题。

sentences.en: And then as soon as they left, I'd be like, oh, so they hate me.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦他们离开，我就会想，哦，所以他们讨厌我。

sentences.en: Oh, so this is over.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以这就要结束了。

sentences.en: Or like, what if this relationship isn't right for me?
sentences.zh: 或者像，万一这段感情不适合我呢？

sentences.en: And I realized that it was because it's so easy to feel safe when there's someone there who's going to constantly validate you,
sentences.zh: 我意识到这是因为，当身边有人不断给予你肯定时，想要感到安全是多么容易，

sentences.en: but you have to be able to validate yourself and able to validate what you know about the relationship, what you know about the other person.
sentences.zh: 但你必须能够肯定自己，能够肯定你对这段感情的了解，对另一个人的了解。

sentences.en: Adding to that list of kind of signs that indicate unhealed trauma, picking fights or starting fights on things that are super arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 补充一下那些表明创伤未愈的迹象，比如为一些极其无理取闹的事情挑起争端或争吵。

sentences.en: Obviously there are, you should be, feel free to express anger, rage, whatever feeling, but there are sometimes things where you're like,
sentences.zh: 显然你可以，你也应该自由地表达愤怒、狂怒或任何情绪，但有时你会想：

sentences.en: I'm going to start this fight because I want to emotionally almost bait this person and see if they're going to leave.
sentences.zh: 我要挑起这场争吵，因为我想在情绪上试探这个人，看看他们会不会离开。

sentences.en: I'm going to, I'm going to bring up something from the, it really doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 我要翻出一些以前的旧账，其实根本无所谓。

sentences.en: I'm actually not bothered by it, but I want to, I want to see how far I can push this person because you're kind of seeking this sense of like, people have left me in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不介意，但我想要看看我能把这个人逼到什么地步，因为你内心在寻找一种感觉，那就是：过去有人离开过我。

sentences.en: People have abandoned me.
sentences.zh: 人们曾经抛弃过我。

sentences.en: I want to know now whether this person is going to be one of those people.
sentences.zh: 我现在想知道这个人会不会是其中之一。

sentences.en: So let's put them through a little bit of a test here.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们给他们设一个小小的考验吧。

sentences.en: I think that is a huge, huge one that we see.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常非常普遍的现象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's something that you actually need to, you need to be really honest about that with yourself because it can become really problematic or worse comes to worse.
sentences.zh: 这是你需要对自己非常诚实的一点，因为它可能会变得非常棘手，或者更糟糕的是，

sentences.en: You actually end up losing them and you, and, and you didn't need to, like, you didn't, this person would have been amazing, but they, but they were like, I don't,
sentences.zh: 你最终真的失去了对方，而这本不必发生——你本没必要这样做，这个人本来会非常棒，但他们却觉得，我受够了，

sentences.en: I don't feel like this is fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不公平。

sentences.en: I don't feel like this is justified.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这没有道理。

sentences.en: They actually have done the healing themselves to know that they deserve maybe something different.
sentences.zh: 他们自己已经做过疗愈，深知自己值得更好的对待。

sentences.en: So part of that is like communication and being like, Hey, actually, I'm not mad about that.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一部分在于沟通，坦诚地说：“嘿，其实我不是在生那个的气。”

sentences.en: I really just wanted to start a fight.
sentences.zh: “我其实只是想挑起争吵。”

sentences.en: Let's unpack that.
sentences.zh: 让我们来剖析一下原因。

sentences.en: How do you communicate with your new partner when you are reacting that way or kind of what you need, whether in those moments where you're trying to nitpick them,
sentences.zh: 当你这样做出反应时，或者当你试图挑刺、把对方推开的那些时刻，你如何与新伴侣沟通你真正需要的是什么？

sentences.en: trying to push them away, what you actually need then?
sentences.zh: 那时你真正需要的到底是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I really relate to this one because it's, it was me in my twenties.
sentences.zh: 所以我和这个很有共鸣，因为我二十多岁的时候就是这样。

sentences.en: Um, and I remember being in a previous relationship where whenever we went on holiday, the third day would always be an argument, always be an argument.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得在上一段感情中，每次我们去度假，第三天总会爆发争吵，总会吵架。

sentences.en: And it will always come from me.
sentences.zh: 而且导火索总是我。

sentences.en: And again, it's a thing of like, this is a fair day with somebody.
sentences.zh: 这又回到了那种心态：这是和某人的快乐的一天。

sentences.en: How do I know if they still want to spend time with me?
sentences.zh: 我怎么知道他们是否还想跟我共度时光？

sentences.en: So let me just like pick at something to see, you know, unconsciously, not kind of specifically, but like unconsciously, it was like, Oh, it's like, it's been so intimate.
sentences.zh: 所以让我挑点刺来看看，你知道，不是刻意的，而是下意识的，就像是，哦，我们之间已经这么亲密了。

sentences.en: Let me, it's almost, does it feel safe?
sentences.zh: 让我来……这真的有安全感吗？

sentences.en: So let me pick at something.
sentences.zh: 所以让我挑点刺吧。

sentences.en: Um, one thing that helped with my relationship now, so we had the most arguments of our entire relationship in the first year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一件事对我和现任的感情有帮助，我们在第一年里吵架的次数占了整段感情的大部分。

sentences.en: We actually don't really argue that much.
sentences.zh: 我们现在其实不怎么吵架了。

sentences.en: Like we do, um, challenge each other, but we, we're not very argumentative couple, but in the first year, loads.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们确实会互相挑战，但我们不是那种经常争吵的情侣，不过在第一年，吵得可多了。

sentences.en: Um, and one thing that we did was we had on our phone, um, because we both relate to conflict in very different ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们做过的一件事是，在手机上——因为我们面对冲突的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: We had on our phone, uh, just a note, which said kind of, um, what do I need when there's conflict and what does he need when there's conflict?
sentences.zh: 我们在手机上建了一个便签，上面写着：当发生冲突时我需要什么，当发生冲突时他需要什么？

sentences.en: So he needs five minutes, 10 minutes to like go reflect, think about things.
sentences.zh: 所以他需要五分钟、十分钟去反思、去思考事情。

sentences.en: Whereas I'm someone that wants to be like, I want answers now.
sentences.zh: 而我是那种迫不及待想要“我现在就要答案”的人。

sentences.en: Um, so then we came across, came across, we kind of had an agreement of what we would do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，后来我们找到了解决办法，达成了一种行动共识。

sentences.en: Let's have 10, 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们给自己10到15分钟。

sentences.en: I write down what I need to write down and then I talk to you about it and then you go away and you respond, let's respond to it.
sentences.zh: 我写下我需要写的东西，然后我跟你谈，接着你走开去消化，我们再对此做出回应。

sentences.en: And another thing that I also tell to clients when they feel triggered in a new relationship is to write down what your triggers are.
sentences.zh: 我还会告诉来访者的另一件事是，当你在一段新恋情中感到被触发时，把你的触发点写下来。

sentences.en: Um, and to share that with your partner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并与你的伴侣分享。

sentences.en: And obviously that list might grow.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个清单可能会变长。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: Um, but to share that with your new partner and also tell them, you know, share on the list what you might need when you are triggered.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但要和你的新伴侣分享这些，还要告诉他们，在被触发时你可能需要什么。

sentences.en: So do you need them to leave you alone?
sentences.zh: 所以你需要他们离你远点吗？

sentences.en: Do you need them to give you a hug?
sentences.zh: 你需要他们给你一个拥抱吗？

sentences.en: Do you need them to say, let's go for a walk?
sentences.zh: 你需要他们说“我们去散步吧”？

sentences.en: Or let me just, you stay in the living room where I'll go and make you something to eat or order us something to eat.
sentences.zh: 还是让我留在起居室，而你去给我做点吃的，或者给我们点个外卖？

sentences.en: Um, whatever it is, you're communicating to them, you know, almost like a first aid kit of what to do when you're triggered.
sentences.zh: 嗯，无论是什么，你都要向他们传达，这几乎就像是一个急救包，告诉你被触发时该怎么做。

sentences.en: Because they're going to be like, oh my gosh, they're triggered.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会觉得，天哪，他们被触发了。

sentences.en: They're angry at me or they're this or this.
sentences.zh: 他们生我的气了，还是怎么着。

sentences.en: What the hell do I do in this situation?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下我到底该怎么办？

sentences.en: So you're at least giving them a toolbox that they can make use of.
sentences.zh: 所以你至少是在给他们提供一个可以利用的工具箱。

sentences.en: And then you're also getting what you need at the same time.
sentences.zh: 同时你也能得到你所需要的东西。

sentences.en: Um, that is such a good suggestion, like such a good skill because I'm the same.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个超级好的建议，真是一个好技巧，因为我也一样。

sentences.en: I'm like, I need you to validate.
sentences.zh: 我会想：我需要你给予肯定。

sentences.en: I need you to tell me it's all okay right now.
sentences.zh: 我需要你告诉我此刻一切都好。

sentences.en: Otherwise, I'm going to lose my fucking shit.
sentences.zh: 否则，我他妈的就要崩溃了。

sentences.en: Like I'm going to panic.
sentences.zh: 就像我会恐慌一样。

sentences.en: Like I'm going to throw up, like not throw up, but I'm just going to feel really upset.
sentences.zh: 我会想吐，倒也不是真的吐，但我就是会觉得很难过。

sentences.en: I'm going to feel really anxious.
sentences.zh: 我会觉得非常焦虑。

sentences.en: I love the idea of that.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个主意。

sentences.en: I also think I'm going to add to this.
sentences.zh: 我想我还要补充一点。

sentences.en: Just if you really struggle with being honest with someone around what's happened in the past, around what you need.
sentences.zh: 如果你实在很难向别人坦诚过去发生了什么、以及你需要什么。

sentences.en: Me and my partner do this thing called vulnerable chats.
sentences.zh: 我和伴侣会进行一种叫做“敞开心扉的聊天”。

sentences.en: Where we'll be like, hey, I want to have vulnerable chats tonight.
sentences.zh: 我们会说：“嘿，今晚我想来一次敞开心扉的聊天。”

sentences.en: Like tonight is the night that we're going to have vulnerable chats.
sentences.zh: “今晚就是我们要进行真诚交流的夜晚。”

sentences.en: And so we both kind of get into a headspace of like, okay, like let's be a little bit nicer to each other.
sentences.zh: 于是我们俩都调整好心态：好吧，我们要对彼此更温柔一点。

sentences.en: Not that we ever mean, but like let's be particularly gentle.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说我们平时刻薄，但就是要特别温柔。

sentences.en: Let's like make this a gentle environment and set ourselves up for success here so that neither person feels, you know, not threatened, but like, yeah,
sentences.zh: 我们要营造一个温柔的环境，为成功打好基础，这样双方都不会感到——也不是受到威胁，而是觉得，对，

sentences.en: threatened by the other person.
sentences.zh: 受到对方的威胁。

sentences.en: Not because the other person is trying to be threatening, but just because they're not prepared for what's happening.
sentences.zh: 倒不是因为对方试图带来威胁，而是因为他们对即将发生的事情毫无准备。

sentences.en: Like they're not prepared for a big reveal or like a big truth session.
sentences.zh: 就像他们没有准备好迎接一次重大的自我剖析或深度坦白局一样。

sentences.en: So I think that that is, but I'm going to use your skill.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这很好，但我也会用你的技巧。

sentences.en: I'm going to use your little tip as well.
sentences.zh: 我也要用你这个小建议。

sentences.en: I think that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。

sentences.en: So I have one final question for you.
sentences.zh: 所以我要问你最后一个问题。

sentences.en: What do you think is your perspective here?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你在这件事上的看法是什么？

sentences.en: Do you need to be fully healed before you enter into a new relationship or can you allow love to heal you or can you heal whilst you're in a new relationship?
sentences.zh: 你需要在完全治愈后才能进入一段新感情，还是可以允许爱来治愈你，或者你可以在新感情中一边治愈自己？

sentences.en: So I don't believe in the idea of anyone being fully healed.
sentences.zh: 所以我不相信任何人能达到完全治愈这种说法。

sentences.en: Yeah, like you read the book, like the first page was like my therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 对，就像你读那本书一样，第一页就写着我的治疗师。

sentences.en: That's why I asked you that question.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我问你那个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's not real.
sentences.zh: 对，那不是真实的。

sentences.en: I'm setting you up for a particular answer.
sentences.zh: 我是在引导你给出一个特定的答案。

sentences.en: So the first page of my, in my book is literally me in therapy and saying, oh my God, I can't wait to be this amazingly fully healed person.
sentences.zh: 所以我的书的第一页，字面意思就是我在做心理咨询，然后说，天哪，我迫不及待地想成为那个神奇的、完全被治愈的人。

sentences.en: It's going to be amazing.
sentences.zh: 那一定会很棒。

sentences.en: I can just like live the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 我就可以这样过完我的余生。

sentences.en: And then my therapist is like, yeah, Tasha, that's not real.
sentences.zh: 然后我的治疗师就说，听着，塔莎，那不是真的。

sentences.en: There's no such thing.
sentences.zh: 根本没有那回事。

sentences.en: And like my jaw dropping and feeling like my parent just told me that Santa Claus doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我的下巴都要惊掉了，感觉就像我父母刚刚告诉我圣诞老人根本不存在一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like, you know, there is no idea of this fully healed person.
sentences.zh: 对，就像是，你知道的，根本没有什么完全被治愈的人这回事。

sentences.en: We are going to be healing and evolving for the rest of our lives right until the very end of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们将在余生中不断疗愈和成长，直到生命的最后时刻。

sentences.en: And I think that's the most beautiful thing about being human is that we are going to be always changing and knowing about ourselves more and more each day.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为作为人类最美妙的事情就是，我们将永远在改变，每一天都在更多地了解自己。

sentences.en: I think it does help to have, it definitely helps to have had some healing work before you go into a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在进入一段感情之前，进行过一些疗愈工作确实有帮助，这绝对是有帮助的。

sentences.en: I would say it's absolutely vital, but it will add some ease into having, you know, self-awareness of, you know, we are part of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 我想说这绝对至关重要，但它会让你在拥有自我意识时感到一些轻松，你知道的，我们都是这段关系的一部分。

sentences.en: If you haven't experienced any healing before a relationship, then, you know, it is going to be tough.
sentences.zh: 如果在恋爱前没有经历过任何疗愈，那么，你知道的，这将会很艰难。

sentences.en: I'm not going to lie.
sentences.zh: 我不会撒谎。

sentences.en: It will be very triggering at times.
sentences.zh: 有时会非常触动心弦。

sentences.en: But it also depends on the person that you're with.
sentences.zh: 但这也要看你和谁在一起。

sentences.en: And maybe they've done some healing work or maybe they have some self-awareness.
sentences.zh: 也许他们做过一些疗愈工作，或者他们有一定的自我意识。

sentences.en: And being in their presence might teach you about your own self-awareness and healing as well.
sentences.zh: 身处他们的陪伴中，可能也会教导你如何认识自我和进行疗愈。

sentences.en: But there are so many, you know, great resources like this podcast and great books.
sentences.zh: 但有那么多，你知道的，很棒的资源，比如这个播客和很棒的书籍。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's so many things that you can access now that even if you are in a relationship and you're like, oh, crap, I haven't done years of therapy yet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，现在你可以接触到很多东西，即使你正在恋爱，然后心里想，天哪，我还没做过多年心理咨询呢。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: You know, it's never too late.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，永远不会太迟。

sentences.en: Just it's about giving yourself grace and space.
sentences.zh: 关键是要给自己留出宽容和空间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Grace.
sentences.zh: 宽容。

sentences.en: I love the idea of grace.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢宽容这个概念。

sentences.en: It's like self-forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对自己的原谅。

sentences.en: Like you are never going to be the best, the best partner.
sentences.zh: 就像你永远不会成为最棒的那个伴侣。

sentences.en: Like you're never going to be a fully perfect partner, parent, friend, colleague, anything.
sentences.zh: 就像你永远不会成为一个完全完美的伴侣、父母、朋友、同事或任何角色。

sentences.en: Like it's always going to be a bit of a work in progress.
sentences.zh: 就像这永远是一个不断完善的过程。

sentences.en: And I love what you said about I don't think you can ever be fully healed.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢你刚才说的，我不认为人能彻底痊愈。

sentences.en: And you can you can approach that and be like, that is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样看待它，然后觉得：这太可怕了。

sentences.en: I'm going to hold back from love because I I remember when I was like dating again after my last relationship, which was terrible.
sentences.zh: 我要对爱退避三舍，因为我还记得我上一段糟糕的感情结束后，当我重新开始约会时。

sentences.en: I was like, I don't want to meet the love of my life as the version of myself I am right now.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我可不想以我现在的这个状态去遇到我的一生挚爱。

sentences.en: I don't think that if I met the love of my life, they would love me because there's so much work to be done.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果我遇到了我的一生挚爱，他们也不会爱我，因为我身上还有那么多需要改进的地方。

sentences.en: And then the more I kind of went on, I was like, well, I don't think that I think that, you know, if they wouldn't be able to love me as well, if I was perfect.
sentences.zh: 然后随着我经历得越来越多，我就想，嗯，我不觉得，我觉得，你知道的，如果我很完美的话，他们可能也无法真正爱我。

sentences.en: Like there are things that I would want to share with them that wouldn't would be messy and would be ugly,
sentences.zh: 比如有些我想与他们分享的事情，它们可能会很混乱，甚至很丑陋，

sentences.en: but I would hope that they would receive that and I would be willing to receive that from them.
sentences.zh: 但我希望他们能接受这一切，我也愿意从他们那里接受这一切。

sentences.en: So I think that's a really beautiful place to end it.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个非常完美的收尾切入点。

sentences.en: Any final thoughts?
sentences.zh: 还有什么最后的想法吗？

sentences.en: No, I guess I was just I was I was just thinking about what you just said and that was a another thing,
sentences.zh: 没有，我想我刚才只是，我只是在思考你刚才说的话，那是另一回事，

sentences.en: but just another thing that can often sabotage us in our relationships is when we're trying to be perfect or trying to be perfect for our partner,
sentences.zh: 但这往往是另一件会破坏我们感情的事，那就是当我们试图表现完美，或者试图在伴侣面前表现完美时，

sentences.en: but not actually be our authentic selves.
sentences.zh: 却没能展现真正的自我。

sentences.en: Um, so allow your partner to see the mess they need to you need to let your message exist together so that you can like kill through it together as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以要让你的伴侣看到那些杂乱，你需要让你们的杂乱共同存在，这样你们也能一起经历并度过难关。

sentences.en: And I think that's really important.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的很重要。

sentences.en: Um, and that's when the real relationship happens is when you can both be really real with each other.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真正的感情就是发生在你俩能向彼此坦诚相待的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's when the real relationship happens.
sentences.zh: 对，真正的感情就是从那时开始的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's like the perfect place to like that is the perfect final message to leave with the listeners.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个完美的切入点，简直是留给听众的完美临别寄语。

sentences.en: Um, I really hope that you enjoyed this episode.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我真的希望你们喜欢这一期节目。

sentences.en: I hope you learned something.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们有所收获。

sentences.en: Tasha, thank you so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 塔莎，非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: That was such an amazing kind of insight.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种非常棒的见解。

sentences.en: Such a great conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常棒的对话。

sentences.en: I feel like I learned a lot.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我学到了很多。

sentences.zh: 听众在哪里能找到你呢？

sentences.zh: 因为你是我最喜欢的创作者之一。

sentences.en: I love your work.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你的作品。

sentences.en: I learn from your work and I think that everyone should have a bit more positivity in their feed.
sentences.zh: 我从你的作品中获益匪浅，我觉得每个人的信息流里都应该多一点正能量。

sentences.en: Where can they find you?
sentences.zh: 他们能在哪里找到你？

sentences.en: On the internet elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 在互联网的其他地方。

sentences.en: So you can find me on Instagram and TikTok as realtalk.therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在Instagram和TikTok上找到我，账号是realtalk.therapist。

sentences.en: Um, and I also have a sub stack and I also have a book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我还有一个Substack和一个。
